experiment.steer: S015 AIR represents synchronization; refusal must track what the backend can EMIT

headline: THE LAST NAMED-ABSENT CONSTRUCT IN AIR, AND THE REFUSAL THAT WAS BLAMING THE WRONG THING. SIMDGROUP now lowers to a real instruction; DEVICE is refused with the construct that DOES carry it named; and the elementwise refusal's stated reason was WRONG -- it blamed the backend when the binding constraint is the program.
what_was_named_absent: AIR receipts recorded for many blocks that 'SIMDGROUP/DEVICE barrier scopes remain UNLOWERABLE and therefore REFUSED'

measured_before_building.why: adding an instruction that does nothing and calling it a closed gap would be exactly the coverage-without-capability this program keeps refusing

within_a_simdgroup.setup: 32 lanes exchange through threadgroup memory, each reading its neighbour's slot
within_a_simdgroup.verdict: NOT LOAD-BEARING at this shape: correct with and without the fence

across_simdgroups.setup: 256 threads, each reading the slot 32 away, which crosses a simdgroup boundary every time
across_simdgroups.verdict: THE PROBE CAN FAIL: ['none', 'simdgroup'] wrong, threadgroup correct

measured_before_building.the_two_probes_together_say_more_than_ei: WITHIN a simdgroup all three arms are exact at 0.0 -- lockstep makes the fence unnecessary. ACROSS simdgroups no-fence is wrong by 9.854 AND simdgroup_barrier is wrong by EXACTLY THE SAME 9.854 while threadgroup_barrier is exact. So the instruction's scope is precisely what its name says: NO EFFECT INSIDE because it is unnecessary, NO EFFECT OUTSIDE because it is out of scope.
measured_before_building.the_control_is_what_makes_the_first_prob: 'all three correct' is worthless unless the test CAN fail. The cross-simdgroup control fails two of three arms by 9.854, so the probe demonstrably detects a missing fence and the earlier all-pass is a result rather than a blind spot.

what_shipped.barrier_msl: one place a lowering asks for the instruction. THREADGROUP and SIMDGROUP return one; DEVICE RAISES and names AirGraph.
what_shipped.simdgroup_is_emitted_but_not_claimed_as_: it is emitted for two reasons that are NOT correctness-on-this-chip: it constrains the COMPILER's reordering, and lockstep is a HARDWARE PROPERTY a future device need not preserve. Calling it a closed synchronization gap would be overreach.
what_shipped.device_refusal_names_the_alternative: device-wide ordering has no in-kernel Metal instruction because IT IS A COMMAND-BUFFER BOUNDARY -- and AIR already expresses that, as an AirGraph dependency EDGE. A refusal that points at the construct which does carry the semantics is worth more than one that only says no.

a_refusal_of_mine_was_blaming_the_wrong_.old_message: 'the Metal backend has no synchronization lowering, and dropping a barrier would silently introduce a race'
a_refusal_of_mine_was_blaming_the_wrong_.why_it_was_wrong: AIR's matmul, softmax and attention lowerings ALL emit threadgroup barriers, and have for many blocks. The backend was never the constraint for those programs.
a_refusal_of_mine_was_blaming_the_wrong_.the_real_constraint: an ELEMENTWISE AIR program declares no threadgroup allocation and no cross-thread reads, so every thread is independent and a barrier of ANY scope HAS NOTHING TO ORDER. The refusal is correct; its stated cause was not.
a_refusal_of_mine_was_blaming_the_wrong_.why_that_matters: a refusal that names the wrong cause teaches the wrong lesson to whoever reads it next -- in this case that the backend cannot synchronize, which would have made the matmul's own barriers look impossible.
a_refusal_of_mine_was_blaming_the_wrong_.the_distinction_that_must_not_rot: two tests sit beside each other: an elementwise program carrying a barrier is REFUSED, a matmul is ACCEPTED because its lowering emits its own. Refusal tracks what the backend can EMIT FOR THIS PROGRAM.

claim_boundary.no_performance_claim: nothing was timed; this is correctness and IR structure only
claim_boundary.simdgroup_lowering_is_not_wired_into_a_p: barrier_msl supplies the instruction and the elementwise path still refuses barriers because it still has nothing to order. No AIR program currently DECLARES a SIMDGROUP barrier and executes -- what closed is the INSTRUCTION and the REFUSAL'S HONESTY, not a new executable program shape.
claim_boundary.one_machine: lockstep within a simdgroup is an M3 Ultra observation at simd width 32; nothing here is promoted to a property of Apple GPUs in general.
claim_boundary.device_stays_absent: DEVICE-scope barriers remain unlowerable and always will be at the instruction level; the routing to AirGraph is a redirection, not a closure.
